text:
ryan: Heads up — CI failing for attention kernels during packaging / image push. Root error in the logs: undefined reference to flash_attn_fused_forward. full log: https://ci.redwood.local/builds/3821

ci-bot: build #3821 failed on runner ubuntu-20.04-gcc11-packager (exit code 1) — see artifacts.

kevin: probably a toolchain/container mismatch. Are we mixing gcc versions between the runtime image and CI matrix?

ryan: Image tag in use: ghcr.io/redwood/attn-runtime:stable-2026-03-16
Dockerfile snippet from that image:
```
FROM ubuntu:20.04
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y build-essential gcc-11 g++-11 cmake ninja-build
```
Link error excerpt:
```
/tmp/build/flash_attn/libflashattn.a(kernel_fused.o): In function `build_kernel':
kernel_fused.cpp:(.text+0x1f2): undefined reference to `flash_attn_fused_forward'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

sasha: Our CI matrix for runtime uses ubuntu-22.04 + gcc-12 for some jobs. Packaging step uses the stable image (gcc-11). That can end up generating artifacts with mismatched libstdc++/mangled symbols. :eyes: Could be ABI mismatch.

maria: Also noticed differing CXXFLAGS between builds: CI test builds use `-O3 -march=native -fPIC`, packager builds use `-O2 -msse4.2`. Different optimization + ABI-friendly flags change inline instantiations in headers and can lead to unresolved symbols at link time.

kevin: I can repro locally by forcing cmake to use gcc-12 vs gcc-11:
```
cmake -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=gcc-12 -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=g++-12 ..
make -j
```
When I mix compilers for object files (some objects compiled with 11, some with 12) I get the undefined refs.

jen: quick mitigation — pin the stable image to gcc-12 and rebuild the packager image so toolchain matches the CI kernels. Also add a CI job that builds and links using the exact image we push.

ryan: There's another symptom: after the image swap some kernel-selection heuristics started preferring paged-attn over fused-attn for shapes we expect fused to win. Profiling traces show spikes in KV cache misses right after the runtime rollout. Not sure if packaging caused a change in kernel behaviour (vectorization differences?), but rollout timing coincides. Trace: https://perf.redwood.local/trace/attn/3821

maria: Vectorization differences from different -march or compiler version can change performance; small codegen differences alter heuristics (latency vs throughput). We should run a small A/B microbench: fused vs paged on representative traces. Add a smoke perf check to CI that fails if throughput drops >5% vs baseline.

ci-bot: Created infra ticket RW-2026 for packager image rebuild and CI matrix updates: https://issues.redwood.local/RW-2026

kevin: I'll take RW-2026. Plan: (1) rebuild ghcr image with gcc-12/g++-12 + consistent CFLAGS, (2) add a packaging sanity job that builds kernels in the same image, (3) add a small ldd/check to ensure libstdc++ is the expected soname, (4) add light perf smoke test for fused vs paged on common shapes.

ryan: dropping raw logs here for folks debugging:
```
[100%] Linking CXX shared library libflashattn.so
/tmp/build/flash_attn/kernel_fused.o: In function `build_kernel':
kernel_fused.cpp:(.text+0x1f2): undefined reference to `flash_attn_fused_forward'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

maria: small note — don't try `-static-libstdc++` as a bandaid, that can break other dynamic libs; prefer keeping GCC major consistent across build/runtime. Also update the README/toolchain doc with the supported matrix (gcc-12+, glibc 2.35+).

jen: I'll add the perf smoke test to the infra repo and wire it into RW-2026. For rollback: can we pin the runtime rollout back to previous image to restore production perf while we fix the packaging?

ryan: yes, rolling back to ghcr.io/redwood/attn-runtime:stable-2026-03-09 mitigates the immediate failures and perf blips. We should still fix CI to prevent future mismatches.

kevin: I'll push a candidate image and open a PR with build logs and local perf numbers. Will also add a CI guard to fail if mixed GCC majors are used during the same link.

sasha: one more thought — add a lightweight kernel-symbol-check step: compare exported kernel symbol sets between images (names + mangling) so we catch missing symbols before pushing.

ryan: agreed. thanks everyone — I'll keep the thread updated with RW-2026 progress and link the PR when ready. :thumbsup:
